title: Device Entered Standby During Enrollment
description: Detects that the device completed a sleep, hibernate or Modern Standby episode of at least 5 minutes while the enrollment was running (system_sleep_episode event from the agent's system timeline watcher, recorded retroactively at wake from the Windows event log). The watcher also backfills pre-agent episodes from the last 24 h for timeline context (backfilled=true); those ended before the enrollment started and are excluded via the same-event filter backfilled equals false — a separate condition could not do that, because each condition scans all events on its own and a pre-session hibernate would still satisfy the duration test. A single required condition keeps the match pinned to one event instance so the interpolated duration is the matched value. Short Modern Standby screen-off scenarios (under 60 s of real sleep) never emit the event, and this rule adds a 5-minute floor so brief lid-close moments do not fire it.
explanation: The device was asleep for {{durationSeconds}} seconds during the enrollment window. Nothing progresses while the device sleeps — downloads pause, the IME stops processing and the ESP simply waits — so the wall-clock enrollment duration includes this pause and can look much slower than the enrollment actually was. The matched system_sleep_episode event in the session timeline carries the exact enter/exit times, the episode kind (sleep, hibernate or Modern Standby) and, for Modern Standby, whether the device was on AC power. A long unexplained gap in the timeline right before that event is this pause, not missing telemetry.

remediation.title: Keep the device awake during enrollment
steps: Check the matched system_sleep_episode event in the timeline for the episode bounds and kind — the enrollment duration minus the episode duration is the real active time.
If the device slept on battery, connect AC power during setup; Windows sleeps far more aggressively on battery.
Instruct users/technicians to keep the lid open and the device powered until the enrollment finishes.
For recurring cases, review the power plan applied during OOBE/ESP (e.g. via provisioning or Intune policy) — consider disabling sleep on AC for the enrollment window.
